## ✨ Highlights

- 🚚 **Log shipping that keeps its place**: the shipper reads only what it hasn't sent, where it used to re-read and re-check the whole current segment at every pass; Elasticsearch documents are built typed, a third of the allocations.
- 🪶 **The Controller's pages load less**: the heavy views come when opened - a node's page starts with half its JavaScript.
- 🏗️ **CI and the runners**: a job of their own for the log tests, the four images of a release from one root filesystem, the docs checked only when they change, a runner that tidies itself.

## ⚙️ Node

- **The log shipper** (`internal/logship`, the LOGS partition): a reader that keeps its place resumes from a mark - the segment and the offset after the last record it took - instead of re-reading 1 MiB and re-checking every record's CRC at every pass, at least twice a flush per target. "Anything new?" on a full segment: 1.29 ms and 21,000 allocations → 117 µs and 5. The segment buffers are pooled; a flush encodes straight into the segment image.
- **Elasticsearch documents** are typed structs, in the same field order as before (a test keeps the old builder and compares the bytes): a bulk of 500 records 10.1 → 5.5 ms, 50,000 → 16,000 allocations. One stated difference: a JSON access log's `haproxy` object is sent as HAProxy wrote it (its key order, its number formatting) instead of decoded and re-encoded with sorted keys - the same JSON.
- Proven on real enforcing nodes: rsyslog over UDP, TCP and TLS with an outage and a reboot, Elasticsearch storing each record once, no AVC denial.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **The heavy views load when opened** (`React.lazy`): on a node's page, Traffic flow, HAProxy, Update, Let's Encrypt, Sysctl, Network configuration and others - 21 views -; on the Controller's page, the Hypervisors, Audit, Backups, Log forwarding, Tokens and Users tabs, the machine console, the CLI sign-in pages and the restore form. The overview and the small monitoring views stay in the first bundle.
  - The Controller's main bundle 471 → 355 KB (gzipped 136 → 108), a node page's 627 → 317 KB (182 → 99), the rest in chunks fetched on demand and cached for a year (v2026.10.20).
  - A chunk that fails to load - a Controller updated under an open page, the old chunk gone - reloads the page once.
- The pages walked in headless Chromium against a real Controller and three nodes, the lazy views included: no error.

## 🧪 Tests and tooling

- **image-build**: a `test-logs` job takes the log, console, kernel-parameter and hot-plug tests out of `test-api` - eleven of its twenty minutes, seven more than any other job; `publish` builds the Proxmox, KVM, VMware and ISO images in **one** `make`, so the four carry the same root filesystem and the same dm-verity root hash (they were built four times before, each a different hash); and it ends by tidying the runner it ran on - the per-commit Controller image tags older than a week, the volumes no container uses, the dangling images. On 2026-10-20 a runner's 64 GB disk full of 124 such tags lost three jobs of v2026.10.20's run; each runner now has an explicit BuildKit cache budget too ([CI runners](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/ci-runners.md)).
- **ci.yml**: the `docs` job in three - `docs-build` always (the Markdown lint, the Astro build, every link), `docs-smoke` only when a change touches the docs, the site, the examples or the proto files (the browser walk of 71 pages: a Go-only pull request no longer waits for it), `examples` always. The browser walk waits for the fonts before measuring a page, which the parallel walk of v2026.10.20 twice caught too early.
- **The Dockerfiles' BuildKit frontend** `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` is pinned by digest (1.27), like every other image: a build in cache no longer asks Docker Hub for it. Bumped by hand ([Upstreams](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/upstreams.md)).
- v2026.10.20's pre-release report: [docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.20.md](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.20.md) - ready to promote.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Nodes**: the usual A/B update; the shipper's marks are in memory, nothing on STATE changes. Elasticsearch documents are the same JSON.
- **The Controller**: update it for the lighter pages. A browser that still holds the old page gets the new one on its next visit.
- **janusctl** and **the Terraform provider**: rebuilt, unchanged.
